gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the Anker SOLIX S5000's headline "10,000 cycles" is measured to 60% capacity, and that on the 80% basis EcoFlow uses for the DELTA Pro 3's 4,000 cycles the S5000 is rated 6,000.
standout_why: Compared against the cited StormWatts solar-input page, which lists the S5000 as a bare "10,000 cycles" with no percentage and gives no cycle life for the other three stations, and against the uncited StormWatts flagship page, which has DELTA Pro 3 at 4,000 cycles to 80% and F3800 Plus at 3,000+ with no percentage but does not cover the S5000. The Anker F3800 Plus bundle page (cited) says only "LFP, 3,000+ cycles". The EcoFlow bundle pages (cited) returned HTTP 429 on every attempt today, so I could not check them. Rivals therefore hold part of the cycle-life table; the S5000 footnote and the same-basis comparison are new.
decides: It confirms the Anker SOLIX S5000 + 2× 400 W kit as the pick: it is the only portable kit we link that ships now and clears 4,000 W continuous (4,500 W rated, link price $3,599.99). Its cycle advantage over the DELTA Pro 3 is 1.5× on the same 80% basis (6,000 vs 4,000), not the 2.5× the headline 10,000 suggests. The BLUETTI Elite 400 kits fit only if the shopper means 4,000 Wh: they are rated 2,600 W (the 3,900 W figure is "Lifting Power") and are pre-orders for mid or late January 2027, so they are the cheaper option for a shopper who can wait, from $1,756.55. The BLUETTI 5kWh RV kits also ship now at 5,000 W but are RV kits (power hub plus separate battery) and cost more per Wh. I could not read the EcoFlow or Jackery bundle prices today, so the price comparison against those rivals is still open.
